newsitem.title: USA: Republic to buy National Car for $600 million.
newsitem.headline: Republic to buy National Car for $600 million.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc. signed a definitive agreement to buy privately held National Car Rental System Inc. in a stock deal worth about $600 million, the two companies said Monday.

The purchase is the second in recent months by Republic, a diversified company operating in the automotive, solid waste, electronic security and media industries. It bought Alamo Rent-a-Car in November.
National is owned by Santa Anna Holdings Inc., an investor group led by William Lobeck, the former chief executive officer of Thrifty Car Rental.
The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close before the end of the first quarter.
Lobeck and senior executives will sign long-term employment agreements with Republic, and will manage National's daily operations, the companies said.

"The addition of National provides Republic with a significant presence in the business and corporate travel segments of the automobile rental industry, which complements Alamo's strong presence in the leisure segment," said H. Wayne Huizenga, Republic chairman and co-chief executive officer.

"The resources that Republic brings to this merger will strengthen our company as well as provide new opportunities, and allow us to serve our customers even better in the future," Lobeck said in a statement announcing the deal.

National, with headquarters in Minneapolis, has about 800 locations in the United States and Canada. Its business is conducted through company-owned, licensed and affiliated operations. The company operates a fleet averaging approximately 100,000 vehicles in the United States.
